---

**THURSDAY 12 Nov — AI + cyber security**

```
Hackers raised the temperature in hundreds of supermarket fridges overnight. The food spoiled.

The controllers were reachable from the open internet. Many were guarded only by default passwords. In France, the attackers used the units' own defrost function.

The same controllers run cold rooms in hospitals and medicine warehouses. The same equipment, the same weak logins, a different consequence.

Researchers later showed an AI coding agent could rebuild the attack on a test device in about 28 minutes, for roughly six dollars. The hard part was never the exploit. It was that the door was already open.

I keep thinking about how much of this is not a technical problem. It is an exposure problem.

Where have you seen internet-facing equipment still running on its factory password?

#CyberSecurity #OTSecurity #IoTSecurity #InternetFacing #SecurityAwareness
```

---

**FRIDAY 13 Nov — AI + non-cyber**

```
A machine tool and a humanoid robot now talk to each other in plain language.

The operator gives an instruction. A planner breaks it into tasks and decides which ones the robot does and which ones the machine does. The robot sets up the workpiece, cleans the machine and moves finished parts.

What struck me was the reason it was built. Not to make the machine faster. To remove the need to rebuild the production line for every new robot.

The robot is not bolted into the factory. It is told what to do.

I have been thinking about that as a design choice. Flexibility bought by making the machine understand instructions, not by rewiring it.

What is the last physical process you saw that was automated without changing the building around it?

#PhysicalAI #Robotics #Automation #Manufacturing #FutureOfWork
```

---

Nothing has been published, captured or scheduled. Both are text only, no images yet. Tell me which to approve and I will run the gates, capture the exact text and set the date.
